name: Black kite
lede: Black kite is a near-black reddish brown named for the bird, measured at the same hex as our library's [[espresso]].

sections.title: In Japan: Kurotobi
sections.body: The name is written 黒鳶, romanized Kurotobi, listed among Japan's traditional colors and naming the black kite, a dark brown bird of prey common across Japan [1]. Our library's [[espresso]] sits at the identical measured hex, two unrelated naming traditions landing on the same dark brown [2]. Further out, [[pale-black-tone]] and [[armada]] sit in the same small cluster [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a match for Black kite in 1,767 of 23,781 paintings, about 7.4 percent, more common than 93 percent of the named colors we track [3]. It peaks in the 1500s, in 194 of 2,231 paintings, 1.3 times the rate expected from that century's share of the archive [3]. Inside a painting it is usually hidden rather than prominent, by lightness rank, in 44 percent of its appearances [3]. Amedeo Modigliani used it most: 5 of his 18 paintings here carry it, 3.9 times his peers' rate [3]. It shares canvases more than chance with colors we call Reddish wine and Dull Orange [3]. The earliest archive match dates to 1210, and our sources give no Western first-recorded date for this traditional Japanese name to compare it against [3]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, read as screen colors, not pigment identifications[3].
